CSTEP Training · for every employee

Raise a request — and claim it back

Travel Claims holds four forms. Tour Proposal and Event Request go in before the trip or event; Local Travel Claim and Expense Claim claim back money you have already spent. This deck fills in each one, end to end, and shows where it goes next.

Part 1 of 6

Before you start

Where requests live, and how to start one.

  1. 1Your dashboard
  2. 2My Tours — everything you have filed
  3. 3Pick one of the four forms
StartStep 1 of 3 · Your dashboard

Travel Claims → Dashboard

Your dashboard shows everything you have in flight: open requests, what is waiting on you, what is waiting on someone else, and what closed this year.

The pipeline underneath follows a request through its stages: Draft / Returned → Submitted → Approved → Arranging → Travel report → With Finance. New request starts a form.

Travel Claims → DashboardNew request
StartStep 2 of 3 · My Tours

My Tours — every request you have filed

Travel Claims → My Tours lists your tour proposals, event requests and claims, with tabs per type and for Drafts. It is empty until you file your first one.

New request here does the same as on the dashboard.

StartStep 3 of 3 · Pick a form

Start a new request: four forms

Tour Proposal — a trip you want arranged. Event Request — hosting or organising an event. Local Travel Claim — local trips and food you have paid for. Expense Claim — other official expenses you have paid for.

Each card lists what you will need. Click Start this form.

Choose the formStart this form
Part 2 of 6

Tour Proposal

Propose a trip — where, when, and the services you need arranged.

  1. 1Traveller (you)
  2. 2Purpose and the project
  3. 3Trip type and dates
  4. 4Stations, one leg per row
  5. 5Services requested
  6. 6Submit — or save a draft
TourStep 1 of 7 · Traveller

You file for yourself

Section 1 fills itself in: your traveller profile, with your Traveller ID — your Employee ID (here NWR-1005) — and your work email.

If it says you have no linked profile, ask your CSTEP Admin to add you as a traveller.

TourStep 2 of 7 · Purpose & project

Pick the project the trip is debited to

Write the Purpose of tour — why you are travelling.

Click Project to be debited: it lists every active project from the Project Master, by code and name. Type to narrow the list.

Purpose of tourProject — pick from the list
TourStep 2 of 7 · Purpose & project

Project picked

The project shows as code — name (here PRJ-SOLAR — Rajasthan Solar Park — Phase 2). Change picks another.

The same picker is on all four forms, so every request and claim is debited to a real project.

TourStep 3 of 7 · Trip & dates

Trip type, dates and time bands

Choose Domestic or International, then the date of departure and date of return, and the time band you prefer for each.

For a domestic trip you can note the date(s) of the event or meeting. International trips add their own sections (funding, forex advance, justification).

TourStep 4 of 7 · Stations

Stations to be visited — one leg per row

One row per leg: From, To and the duration of stay. Add station / leg adds another.

An international trip asks for Countries to be visited instead, each with its dates.

From · To · StayAdd station / leg
TourStep 5 of 7 · Services

The services you need arranged

Pick every mode of travel you need, then say whether you need transport and accommodation — each Yes opens a line for the details.

Add your meal preference, and whether the trip is sponsored.

TourStep 6 of 7 · Submit

Save a draft, or submit for approval

Other details is for anything else the desk should know.

Submit for approval sends it to your Approver. Save draft keeps it to finish later — a draft is checked like a submission, so the required fields must be filled.

Save draftSubmit for approval
TourStep 6 of 7 · Submit

Submitted — the request page

You land on the request: status SUBMITTED, the dates and duration, What you asked for, and the Audit trail — append-only, every action with who and when.

Until it is approved you can Withdraw or Cancel it. Printable form and Download PDF give the formal copy. On approval it gets its Tour TIN (e.g. 0001/1026).

TourStep 7 of 7 · Filing for someone else

CSTEP Admin: search the traveller

A CSTEP Admin can file on anyone's behalf: section 1 becomes a search by name or email.

Each match shows the person's Traveller ID (their Employee ID) — here Meera Pillai — NWR-1006.

TourStep 7 of 7 · Filing for someone else

The traveller is set

Pick the person; their Traveller ID and email show in the section, and × clears it.

Everything else is filled in exactly as for your own request.

Part 3 of 6

Event Request

Propose hosting or organising an event.

  1. 1Title and the project
  2. 2Scope: nature, participants, host, dates, location
  3. 3Registration and funding
  4. 4Logistics
  5. 5Submit
EventStep 1 of 4 · Title & project

The event's title and project

Section 1 is you, the proposer. In section 2 give the title of the event and the project it is accounted to.

The Proposal summary on the right fills in as you go.

EventStep 2 of 4 · Scope

Nature, participants, host, dates, location

Pick the nature of the event — Workshop, Conference, Seminar or Other — and list the participating organisations with a headcount each (Add organisation adds a row; the total is counted).

Then the host institution, the start and end dates, and the location.

NatureParticipants + countsHost · dates · location
EventStep 3 of 4 · Funding & logistics

Registration, funding and logistics

Registration & funding: any registration fee, whether participants present papers, and the project funds available.

Logistics: the venue, whether travel & accommodation support is needed, and the lunch and dinner counts.

EventStep 4 of 4 · Submit

Submitted

Submit for approval and the event request opens with its details and audit trail.

On approval it gets its EVR reference (e.g. EVR0001/1026).

Part 4 of 6

Local Travel Claim

Claim back local trips and food — with a bill per trip, or the no-bill declaration.

  1. 1Purpose, project and claim period
  2. 2Travel lines — a bill, or no bill
  3. 3Food and other expenses
  4. 4The declaration
  5. 5Submit
Local claimStep 1 of 5 · Purpose & period

What the trips were for, and when

Give the purpose of the claim and the project it is debited to.

Set the claim period — every line below must fall inside these dates. The Claim totals on the right update as you add lines.

Local claimStep 2 of 5 · Travel lines

One line per trip — with its bill, or none

Each trip: date, from, to, the mode (cab, local taxi, metro, bus, own vehicle) and the fare. Add trip adds a line.

Attach bill for the trip (trip 1 here). Where there is no bill, tick No bill — add to declaration (trip 2).

Date · from · to · mode · fareAttach bill — or No bill
Local claimStep 3 of 5 · Food & other

Food, other expenses and advance

Food: meals paid for on official work — Add meal, the date and amount; a bill is optional.

Other expenses covers anything not listed above, and Advance taken is netted off what you are owed.

Local claimStep 4 of 5 · Declaration

The declaration — trips with no bill

Every trip marked No bill is listed under Declaration. Submitting the claim is your declaration that these were spent on official work and that no supporting documents exist.

The totals show the amount due by CSTEP — paid to you once the claim is approved and verified.

Local claimStep 5 of 5 · Submit

Submitted

The claim opens with its travel lines (each marked Bill or No bill), food, totals and audit trail.

On approval it gets its LTC reference (e.g. LTC0001/1026); then the CSTEP Admin verifies it and Finance reimburses you.

Part 5 of 6

Expense Claim

Claim back other official expenses, with the tax and the tax invoice.

  1. 1Purpose, project (bill to) and claim period
  2. 2Expense lines
  3. 3Tax, tax invoice and advance
  4. 4Submit
ExpenseStep 1 of 4 · Purpose & period

Purpose, project and period

Give the purpose of the claim, the project (bill to) and the claim period.

Every expense must fall inside these dates.

ExpenseStep 2 of 4 · Expenses

One line per expense, before tax

Each expense: date, description and the amount before tax. Add expense adds a line.

Attach each line's invoice — or attach one tax invoice for the whole claim in the next section.

ExpenseStep 3 of 4 · Tax & invoice

Tax, the tax invoice and any advance

Enter the IGST / other tax on the invoice and any advance taken, and Attach tax invoice — GSTIN and HSN are read from it.

A claim needs an invoice: on each line, or for the whole claim here.

TaxAttach tax invoiceSubmit
ExpenseStep 4 of 4 · Submit

Submitted

The claim opens with its expenses, Totals (as claimed) — subtotal, tax, total, advance — and the audit trail.

On approval it gets its EXP reference (e.g. EXP0001/1026).

Part 6 of 6

After you submit

Drafts, My Tours, and following a request through.

  1. 1Save a draft
  2. 2Edit a draft
  3. 3My Tours — tabs, statuses and actions
  4. 4Your dashboard
AfterStep 1 of 3 · Drafts

Save draft — finish it later

Save draft keeps a request without sending it. It is checked like a submission, so the required fields must be filled.

Use it when a detail — a date, a cost — is still to be confirmed.

AfterStep 1 of 3 · Drafts

A draft: Edit, then submit

The draft opens with status DRAFT and an Edit button. Edit it, then Submit for approval when it is ready.

A request your Approver returns comes back the same way, for you to fix and resubmit.

AfterStep 2 of 3 · My Tours

My Tours — your requests at a glance

The cards count total requests, what is waiting on you (drafts, returns, travel reports), what is in progress with an approver, the desk or Finance, and what is closed.

Filter by type — Domestic, International, Event, Local Travel Claims, Drafts — or search by purpose or ID.

AfterStep 2 of 3 · My Tours

Each row: status and actions

Every request shows its type, purpose and project, dates and status.

The actions follow the status: Edit a draft, Withdraw or Cancel before approval, View any time.

AfterStep 2 of 3 · My Tours

The Drafts tab

Drafts shows only what you have not sent yet — a quick way back to finish them.

AfterStep 3 of 3 · Your dashboard

Your dashboard, now with requests

The dashboard counts your open requests, what is waiting on you and what is waiting on someone else.

The pipeline shows how many of yours sit at each stage — here one draft and four submitted, with the Approver.

Reference

The four forms at a glance

What each form is for, what it asks, and the reference it gets on approval.

FormWhenYou fill inReference on approval
Tour ProposalBefore a tripPurpose, project, trip type and dates, stations / countries, servicesTour TIN — 0001/MMYY
Event RequestBefore an eventTitle, project, nature, participants, host, dates, location, funding, logisticsEVR0001/MMYY
Local Travel ClaimAfter local tripsPurpose, project, period, trips (bill or no bill), food, other, advanceLTC0001/MMYY
Expense ClaimAfter other expensesPurpose, project, period, expenses, tax, tax invoice, advanceEXP0001/MMYY
Recap

You can raise and claim

Pick the right form
Tour or Event before; Local Travel or Expense Claim after the money is spent.
Project on every form
Pick it from the list — it is what the request is debited to.
Bills and invoices
Attach the bill per trip, or mark No bill and it goes into the declaration. An Expense Claim needs its tax invoice.
Follow it in My Tours
Status and actions on every row; drafts and returns wait on you.
